text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.93% today, extending a downward move over the past few days after reaching $134.89 on August 20th. The decline reflects broader weakness in oil prices, which dropped more than 3% on August 25th when the U.S. signaled it would pursue economic pressure against Iran rather than military action—a development that reduced immediate concerns about disruption to Middle Eastern energy supplies. Recent talks between Iran and Oman about managing a joint shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz have also eased tension around one of the world's most critical chokepoints for oil transit.

With geopolitical risk in the Middle East appearing to ease rather than escalate, the pressure that had lifted energy stocks earlier in the month has reversed. Oil refiners and producers benefit from uncertainty and supply constraints, so a shift toward diplomatic resolution and reduced military risk typically weighs on their valuations.
